verdict.reasoning: Patient reports: "I've got a really bad headache, had it for about a day now" and describes it as "kind of throbbing... quite intense".

Location: "mainly on the left side". Quality: "kind of feels like it's throbbing". Course: "just kind of fades, so it's still there a little bit but, it kind of gets more or less, severe" (fluctuating but persistent).
Patient states: "yeah, quite sensitive to light" which is photophobia.
Doctor: "any problems with your eyes, or your eyesight?" Patient: "Uh, no, not at all."
Doctor: "Any, any nausea, vomiting?" Patient: "Uh, no, no, been feeling fine actually."
Doctor: "Is it worse when you lie flat, or when you bend forward?" Patient: "Um, no, think I've generally been lying down, seems to be better that way."
Position: Patient denies worse with lying or bending. Cough: "Any problems if you cough or sneeze?" Patient: "Uh, no". So not affected by bending or coughing.
Onset: "ever since yesterday morning, since I woke up really."
Doctor asks about fever/runny nose/sore ears; patient: "No, not really any sort of, cold symptoms, I seemed OK the day before."
Doctor: "have you been eating and drinking OK?" Patient: "Yeah, yeah" and again later "Yeah, yeah, fine."

"Normally, do you get any headaches?" Patient: "Uh, no not really, it's not something I've, ever had before." Doctor summarizes: "this headache is new to you, and you've, you've not had regular headaches before?" Patient: "Yeah."
Patient only says: "may have been a bit stressed out at work"; no explicit statement that stress is a trigger for this headache.
Cycle: Doctor: "has it occurred at a particular term in your menstrual cycle?" Patient: "no, not particularly, and my period was about a week ago."
Doctor: "Have you had any significant medical problems? Any hospital admissions, operations, something like that?" Patient: "Uh, no, not recently, nothing." No other PMH given.
In the same exchange patient denies "hospital admissions, operations" with "no, not recently, nothing."

For current meds: "Do you take any medication?" Patient: "Uh, no, just contraception." For this headache: "What tablets have you been taking already, for it?" Patient: "Uh, just Paracetamol." Paracetamol is being used as needed.
Patient: "Microgynon, pill." Doctor: "When did you start that one?" Patient: "Uh, about six years ago." Microgynon is a COCP.
Patient: "I'm allergic to Aspirin, so I haven't been taking that." Doctor: "What happens when you take Aspirin?" Patient: "Um, I just feel really sick."
Patient: "my mum had, uh, high blood pressure, and she's got a history of migraines."
Doctor: "who do you live with at home?" Patient: "Uh, just with housemates, um, just friends."
Alcohol: "I'd say a normal amount, um, probably, you know, a few drinks at the weekend."
Doctor: "And do you smoke?" Patient: "No."
Doctor: "Do you take any other drugs of any sort?" Patient: "No."
Temp: "Have you checked your temperature at all?" Patient: "Um, I haven't. Um, I don't feel like I'm feverish, but I haven't checked."
Neuro: "any problems with weakness, tingling, numbness in your arms or legs?" Patient: "No, not at all."
Skin: "Have you had any changes in your skin?" Patient: "No, skin feeling fine."
BP: Patient: "I haven't actually, no." Then: "probably about six months ago" when checking for repeats, and "it's always been fine I think." No current reading given.

Headache described as unilateral ("mainly on the left side"), throbbing, with photophobia and no focal neuro symptoms (denies weakness/tingling/numbness). Doctor: "it does, sound quite like a migraine"—a primary headache.

While COCP use and family history of migraine are documented and doctor says it "sound[s] quite like a migraine", the specific diagnostic formulation "migraine without aura" and linking it as a consideration due to COCP plus family history is not explicitly stated.
BP status unknown currently (last ~6 months ago, "always been fine I think"); onset "ever since yesterday morning, since I woke up" with patient denying fever or other systemic/URI symptoms.

Doctor: "What I would, suggest is, taking, uh, um, some anti-inflammatories, along with the Paracetamol." And patient is known to be aspirin-intolerant, so avoiding aspirin is appropriate and consistent with the plan.
Transcript includes advice for hydration ("Make sure you're really well hydrated") and positional relief is noted, but there is no explicit advice to rest "in a dark, quiet room."
Doctor: "I would, try and arrange to get your blood pressure checked" and "thing to do is to have a thermometer at home, so you can make sure that your temperature's OK."

Safety netting given: seek help if headache not settling/getting worse/any change, high temperature, or rash: "if it, if it isn't settling, or it's getting worse, or you get any other change in your headache. Um, or you're unwell with it, with a high temperature... or you develop any rashes." No mention of new neurological deficits, visual changes, persistent vomiting, or no improvement as distinct criteria.

Doctor: "if you're getting persistent, um, headaches, or headaches associated with your menstrual cycle, or certain things seem to trigger these headaches. Then, it, it would be worth, having a further discussion about it, to see whether we can, work out if we can help the, that longer-term." This implies review to discuss diagnosis/management and triggers.
